# Tier `ampere-16`

## Serving

| setting | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `cuda` | which `llama-swap.*.yaml` template renders |
| ctx_size | 131072 | the served window (`--ctx-size`) |
| kv_type | `q8_0` | `--cache-type-k/v`, kept symmetric |
| flash_attn | `on` | `--flash-attn` (required for a q8_0 V cache) |
| resident_tier | `offload-e4b` | the model that stays hot; seeds the agent planner seat (agent_model) when it differs from the workhorse |
| agent_ctx_tokens | 131072 | the agent's `-ctx-tokens` compaction budget |
| 26B-A4B | dropped | whether the 26B MoE is served, and where its experts live |

## Agent seat

This tier declares a persistent **vLLM** agent seat, and the installer RENDERS it — the
llama-swap entry, the start/stop wrappers and the harness `agent_model` binding all derive from
one declaration, so the seat and the lane routing to it cannot disagree.

| setting | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| id | `qwen3.5-4b-vllm` | the llama-swap model id, `--served-model-name`, and what `agent_model` binds to |
| cards | `0` | `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, in PCI order |
| tensor_parallel | 0 | `--tensor-parallel-size`; must equal how many cards are listed |
| max_model_len | 131072 | the served window |
| kv_cache_dtype | `fp8_e5m2` | KV precision — backend-dependent, not free everywhere |
| ttl_seconds | 300 | idle window before the seat unloads and frees its cards |
| launch | `—` | which artifact set starts it |
| fallback | `qwen3.5-4b-agent` | the llama.cpp seat a box WITHOUT the vLLM venv serves instead |

> NVIDIA A2 16 GB (Lenovo M720q, 40 W / 1200 MHz lock), vLLM 0.28 / torch 2.13+cu130, harness 0.113.19, 2026-09-06. GO decided 16:49; production seat built 23:2x-23:4x. 8/8 digests through the fleet node at a 45 s median (walls 33/33/33/39/45/48/48/51) against the llama.cpp 4B seat's 159 s at 32k -- 3.5x faster at 4x the window; go/no-go rule (8/8 AND >=2x window at <=1.3x wall) held at 0.28x. Weights 4.48 GiB, KV 2.91 GiB -> a 180,098-token pool (1.37x concurrency at 131,072), healthy in 126 s cold / 35 s warm, card 8,536 MiB at 16.7 W idle and 9,148 MiB under load, ~5.8 GB left for the small seats. KxN gate 48/48: K=1 96.7 s (was 121.2), K=2 150.3 s (was 187.8), K=3 190.0 s (was 353.7), 0 refusals. Records: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-09-06-a2-vllm-seat/ (README.md, digest8-qwen3.5-4b-vllm-r1.json) and ADR 0035.

## Media

This tier serves these media **seats** — models in its own llama-swap config, rendered
at install time. Each seat also produces the harness config binding that routes to it, so a
binding can never name a seat that was not rendered:

| seat | kind | binds | model | residency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen38-27b-vision` | vision | `vision_model` | `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-IQ3_S.gguf` | swappable |
| `whisper-stt` | stt | `stt_model` | `ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin` | swappable |

A seat still needs its weights on the box — model downloads stay out-of-band, as with
every seed.

The installer seeds this tier's media bindings (`config_seed`):

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `imagegen_ckpt` | `hidream_o1_image_bf16.safetensors` |
| `imagegen_family` | `hidream-o1` |
| `imagegen_timeout_sec` | `3600` |
| `imagegen_vae` | `builtin` |
| `upscale_model` | `4x-UltraSharp.pth` |
| `videogen_frames` | `81` |
| `videogen_height` | `720` |
| `videogen_text_encoder` | `umt5_xxl_fp16.safetensors` |
| `videogen_timeout_sec` | `5400` |
| `videogen_unet_high` | `Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-HighNoise-Q8_0.gguf` |
| `videogen_unet_low` | `Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-LowNoise-Q8_0.gguf` |
| `videogen_width` | `1280` |

`__OFFLOAD_HOME__` is replaced with the install root at render time.

These `config_seed` keys are applied to a FRESH harness config exactly like the media

here so they are never mistaken for a media capability:

## Operator notes

Recorded with the profile — several are measurements from real hardware,
including reasons a tempting change was deliberately not made.

> Ampere >=12GB band (3090-class defensive). 26B resident full-GPU. config_seed: quality-first media bindings (bf16 needs no fp8 hardware; verified on the 16GB Blackwell tier — needs the model downloads + >=~48GB system RAM). PROJECTED - H3 confirms OOM ceiling. J-media 2026-07-28: same qwen3-vl-8b seat as the MEASURED blackwell-16, but ctx trimmed 16384->8192 because this band's FLOOR is 12GB ('3090-class defensive') and KV has to fit there too; a 24GB 3090 can raise it. ~10GB seat, swappable so it never shares with another heavy seat. PROJECTED on this exact silicon. The 'ocr' alias rides on this shared VLM (one seat owns screenshots/GUI/document OCR); the harness routes via vision_model, not the alias, so it is a label rather than a separate model. TIER-DOCTRINE PASS 2026-08-16: agent seat pointed at the VALIDATED thinking-on 26B agent entry (0/15->12/15 at D1 with reasoning on, 2026-08-10) instead of the derived reasoning-off cascade seat (measured 0% as agent). Same weights as the 26B — no new download. Capability parity with the twin-arch sibling(s) is field-identical by design; the arch split (sm86/sm120/sm70) is a BUILD concern only. MEASURED 2026-09-04 on the NVIDIA A2 16 GB (Lenovo M720q, 40 W / 1200 MHz lock, harness 0.113.9, 8 digest contracts forced-remote): qwen3.5-4b-agent 8/8 median 159 s; gemma4-12b-agent 8/8 median 237 s (kept as an opt-in llama-swap alias); gemma4-26b-agent 1/8 with seven 300 s timeouts (--n-cpu-moe 16, ~9.4 GB VRAM + ~7 GB host) -> the projected 26B seed was WRONG for this band: resident_tier offload-e4b, 26B dropped, agent seat qwen3.5-4b-agent with the research profile (same lever as ampere-6/8). A 24 GB 3090-class card at full power may re-enable the 26B by hand; the seed stays on what a 15 GB / 40 W card measured. MEASURED 2026-09-06 on the same box (harness 0.113.19): the reference deployment moved its agent lane to a persistent vLLM seat behind llama-swap (Qwen3.5-4B w4a16, fp8_e5m2 KV, 131,072-token window, util 0.65, text-only) — 8/8 digests at 45 s median vs 159 s on the llama.cpp 4B seat, 4x the window; that seat is a hand-installed venv + systemd unit, NOT something this seed renders, so the seed keeps qwen3.5-4b-agent / 32768 and the tier page points at ADR 0035 + setup/templates/vllm-seat/linux-systemd/ for the pattern. SERVED WINDOW RAISED 32768 -> 131072 (0.113.32, 2026-09-07). Operator rule, stated three times: install defaults follow the measurement. Holding this seed at 32768 because 'no installer path renders the vLLM seat' was the wrong call -- the fix is to render the seat, not to ship a smaller number than the hardware was measured at. MEASURED on the reference A2 16 GB at its shipped 40 W / 1200 MHz lock: the vLLM seat (Qwen3.5-4B w4a16, vLLM 0.28, fp8_e5m2 KV -- free on Ampere) serves max_model_len 131,072 with a 356,721-token GPU KV pool at 11,888 MiB, fans out to 293 tok/s at 32 streams with 0 failures and a p95 TTFT of 9.25 s, and answers the harness's own 8-digest set 8/8 at a 45 s median against the llama.cpp 4B seat's 159 s (ADR 0035). The rendered llama.cpp seat fits the larger window on the same card because Qwen3.5's Gated-DeltaNet hybrid KV barely grows with context -- measured on the 8 GB sibling, the 9B went 6344 MiB at 16K to 6696 MiB at 32K, only +352 MiB for a doubled window. selftest's ctx canary is the on-box gate if a deployment disagrees. AGENT SEAT RENDERED 2026-09-07 (0.113.33): this tier now declares a `vllm_seat` and the installer RENDERS it -- the systemd unit, the two llama-swap wrappers, the polkit rule and the llama-swap entry -- instead of pointing at a runbook. ADR 0035 originally recorded 'the tier SEED is unchanged: the seat is a hand-installed venv and unit, not something the installer renders', and the consequence was that every fresh ampere-16 install kept getting qwen3.5-4b-agent, the arm that LOST its own bake-off (8/8 at 159 s vs the vLLM seat's 8/8 at 45 s, 4x the window). Operator ruling 2026-09-07: install defaults follow the measurement, so render the seat. PREREQUISITES ARE NOT RENDERED and that is deliberate: the engine is a hand-built venv (vLLM 0.28, torch 2.13+cu130) plus an HF snapshot, so the installer DETECTS them and falls back to the llama.cpp seat with a stated reason when they are absent -- a unit pointing at a venv nobody built fails at boot, which is strictly worse than the fallback. THE RENDERED UNIT IS `vllm-agent-seat`, NOT the reference box's hand-installed `vllm-a2-seat`: a tier is a hardware class and must not name a unit after one machine's card. A box already running vllm-a2-seat keeps it -- running the installer there would create a SECOND unit on the same port, so stop and disable the old one first (`systemctl disable --now vllm-a2-seat`) or leave that box hand-managed. The deployment paths (stack/seat/venv dirs, HF home) are NOT tier fields either: they come from the install root and the box, because hardening one host's layout into a hardware tier is the mistake this table exists to avoid. SEAT JUSTIFICATION CORRECTED 2026-09-08 — THE EARLIER ONE WAS A SPEED ARGUMENT AND IS WITHDRAWN. The 2026-09-04 bake-off's score was `not deferred AND len(findings)>=3 AND len(summary)>40` -- a SHAPE check, which the harness's own acceptance linter classifies as SHAPE-ONLY ('passes garbage'). Both the 4B and the 12B cleared it 8/8, so 8/8 never meant 'equal quality', it meant 'both emitted well-formed output'; the seats were then separated on wall time, which is not a quality signal and is explicitly not how seats are chosen here. BLIND RE-EVALUATION 2026-09-08 on the RETAINED answers (they survived in the digest8-*.json records): the same 8 ADR-digest contracts, judged against the ground-truth ADRs by 3 independent lenses (faithfulness / substance / consumer-usefulness) = 24 judgements, candidates anonymised and order permuted per contract, with no model name, parameter count, engine or timing visible to any judge. Mean overall out of 10 -- qwen3.5-4b-vllm 7.58 (specificity 8.17, coverage 7.12, 0 filler findings, 12 of 24 firsts); qwen3.5-4b-agent llama.cpp 6.79 (7.29 / 6.21, 3 filler, 7 firsts); gemma4-12b-agent 6.38 (6.62 / 5.88, 1 filler, 5 firsts). All three lenses agreed on the ordering. So the vLLM seat IS the quality winner on this task shape and the binding stands -- but on quality evidence, not on 45 s vs 159 s. NUANCE THAT THE MEAN HIDES: the 12B fabricates least SEVERELY (its errors are vagueness and overstatement) while both 4Bs invent specifics, and the llama.cpp 4B inverted a NUMBER (asserting a '5-minute lease timeout' where the ADR says contract timeout + 5 minutes) -- the worst failure kind for a delegated digest. TWO THINGS THIS DOES NOT SHOW, both open: (1) it is ONE task shape, digesting an ADR into findings, and says nothing about longer reasoning, code or multilingual work; (2) THE 12B HAS NEVER RECEIVED THE vLLM TREATMENT. The engine alone moved the SAME 4B weights from 6.79 to 7.58 and removed every filler finding, which is a large effect, so a 12B served under vLLM (w4a16 or Q4, fp8_e5m2 KV) at a reduced window is the untested arm and is the next measurement this tier needs -- the llama.cpp 12B measured 7,512 MiB, so it plausibly fits at util ~0.85 with a 32-64k window. SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY — THE 12B WAS RUN. gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct was already on the box (8.0 GB) and had been all along. Two spec defects had to be fixed to launch it (0.113.37): --limit-mm-per-prompt listed only image and video, so Gemma-4's audio tower was built anyway and vLLM died with AttributeError: 'Gemma4UnifiedAudioFeatureExtractor' object has no attribute 'fft_length'; and fp8_e5m2 KV is NOT free on Ampere but per-BACKEND (FlashAttention works for Qwen3.5, Triton refuses for Gemma-4 on the SAME card: 'native FP8 (fp8e4nv) requires SM89+'). It then needed util 0.95 to serve 32,768 (8.28 GiB weights, KV pool 48,925 tokens, 14,140 MiB) -- a 32k window where the 4B gets 131k on the same card. BLIND FOUR-WAY RESULT (same 8 contracts, same 3 lenses, 4 candidates per packet, Latin-squared, nothing about model/engine/timing visible to any judge), mean overall /10: qwen3.5-4b-vllm 7.75, qwen3.5-4b-agent 7.38, gemma4-12b-vllm 6.50, gemma4-12b-agent 6.21. The 2x2 separates the effects: ENGINE +0.38 on the 4B and +0.29 on the 12B; MODEL -1.17 on llama.cpp and -1.25 on vLLM. So the winning engine did NOT rescue the 12B -- it is worse by ~1.2 on BOTH engines and took 1 of 24 firsts, with all three lenses agreeing. The binding stands on QUALITY. What this still does not show: one task shape, and these are different model FAMILIES rather than sizes (Qwen3.5-4B vs Gemma-4-12B) -- Qwen3.5-9B-quantized.w4a16 is on the box if that is worth settling. The 12B does fabricate least severely (2 distinct vs 5-6), which matters where inventing beats omitting. Evidence: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-09-08-a2-seat-quality-reeval/. VISION SEAT MEASURED 2026-09-12 (0.116.1): qwen3-vl-8b (a J-media inheritance from blackwell-16, never run on this silicon) -> qwen38-27b-vision, Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ3_S + mmproj-F16 at ctx 8192, reasoning off, 12.4 GiB resident. Bake-off through the harness's own assess_image / ocr / vqa over a labelled set on the reference A2 (two phases, the second built to separate candidates the first could not): the 27B was the only candidate that read every serial number, email and low-contrast string (OCR 9/9) with 5/5 VQA; gemma4-12b is the fast runner-up (3 s vs 14 s median, one miscount, one strict brief); qwen3.5-9b FABRICATED text twice and is disqualified for OCR; the box's previous gemma4-e4b-vision missed small-print codes and deferred once. Chosen on QUALITY per the tier doctrine; the 14 s median is the cost of the 40 W lock and is acceptable for QA of renders, which is what the fleet vision lane (ADR 0040) carries. NOT propagated to blackwell-16 / volta-16 / blackwell-2x16: their qwen3-vl-8b Q8 seat was not in this bake (the 8B weights were not on the box), so nothing has measured the 27B against it on a 16 GB card -- that comparison is the open follow-up before any 16 GB sibling inherits this seat. Caveat that pre-exists this change: a seat bigger than the E4B cannot co-reside with the vLLM agent seat while that is loaded; a vision call arriving then defers gpu_busy. Evidence: Benchmarks and Optimizations/2026-09-12-a2-vision-bakeoff/ (results.jsonl, results2.jsonl, labels, drivers).
